item.title: Donegal Expands ZestyAI Property Risk Capabilities
item.description: “The carriers pulling ahead are the ones whose decisions rest on data they can defend.” ZestyAI says it has received more than 500 regulatory approvals nationwide for its property-risk models and related capabilities. (Image source: IIR.) Donegal Insurance Group (Marietta, Pa.) has expanded its relationship with ZestyAI (San Francisco), adding the vendor’s Z-PROPERTY solution to support property-level underwriting and portfolio decisions across its personal lines business. With Z-PROPERTY, Donegal is extending that approach to additional property characteristics including roof condition, roof complexity, lot debris and other features that can affect risk and premium.

item.title: Cotality Launches Supplement Claims Workflow Portal
item.description: “Cotality Supplement solves this conflict with a single, transparent workflow.” Looking Beyond Individual Supplements Cotality says the portal also provides analytics around supplement volume, costs and recurring causes, giving claims leaders greater visibility into patterns that may be driving repeated requests. (Image source: IIR.) Cotality (Irvine, Calif.) has launched Cotality Supplement , a configurable white-label portal designed to streamline property claims supplement workflows between carriers and contractors. Cotality Supplement automatically routes requests to the appropriate claims team and generates side-by-side variance reports showing changes between original and supplemental estimates, including additions, removals and pricing differences.

item.title: Malibu Life, Legacy Launch Two Fixed Indexed Annuities
item.description: (Image source; Malibu Life homepage.) Malibu Life , through its insurance subsidiary TruSpire Retirement Insurance Company (Irving, Texas), and Legacy Marketing Group (Petaluma, Calif.) have announced the launch of PillarMark with MultiRider and SpireMark with MultiRider Max, two fixed indexed annuities designed to address different retirement income needs. The products mark the launch of Malibu’s U.S. “Retirement looks different for every individual, and we believe the products we bring to market should reflect that,” comments Todd Shriber, CEO, Malibu Life.

item.title: World Food Programme buys parametric tropical cyclone insurance from CCRIF
item.description: CCRIF SPC, the regional parametric risk pool for the Caribbean and Central America, has announced that the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has become the first UN agency and multilateral organisation to join and purchase parametric insurance from it. WFP has purchased two parametric tropical cyclone policies to cover the Dominican Republic and Haiti from CCRIF, with the insurance having a combined coverage limit of US $11.6 million. The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has been utilising parametric risk transfer as a way to secure disaster contingent financing to support its operations for nearing two decades.

item.title: Moody’s establishes casualty risk intelligence group with six founding organisations
item.description: Moody’s, a global provider of financial data, risk analysis and business intelligence, has established the Moody’s Casualty Risk Intelligence Group (MCRIG), an initiative involving six founding organisations from across the insurance industry. We are proud to launch the MCRIG in New York and to do so with such a strong and diverse group of founding participants.” Noel Richardson, Chief Risk Officer at AXA XL, added: “Casualty insurance faces significant complexity from emerging risks such as PFAS and AI liability, yet the industry relies largely on backward-looking analysis. Joe Melly, Managing Director and Head of Casualty and Financial Lines at Moody’s, commented: “Casualty insurance is the next frontier for risk analytics, and Moody’s is committed to leading that transformation.

item.title: Renew Risk expands solar farm catastrophe modelling to all 48 contiguous US states
item.description: Renew Risk, a specialist provider of risk analytics for renewable energy and energy demand assets, has expanded its severe convective storm (SCS) modelling capabilities for solar farms to cover all 48 contiguous US states. As the industry expands, Renew Risk is adapting its modelling to reflect changes in the size, location and technical design of solar installations. Renew Risk’s expanded model enables insurers, reinsurers and brokers to assess three key severe convective storm hazards across the contiguous United States.

item.title: W.R. Berkley projects reinsurance contraction of up to 20% amid ‘challenging’ market conditions
item.description: Berkley Corporation is bracing for a continued pullback in its assumed reinsurance operations, warning that deteriorating market conditions across both casualty and property lines will likely drive a double-digit contraction in segment volume over the foreseeable future. He said: “I guess there’s no point in crying any further over spilt milk, but when the day’s all done, as you have heard us talk about for several quarters now, there’s a dissatisfaction with market conditions within casualty, reinsurance, and property. As the reinsurance market remains competitive, Berkley is keen on maintaining underwriting discipline, which is reflected in the segment’s net premiums written declining 11.6% to $369 million, driven by casualty and, to a lesser extent, property.

item.title: Illinois Company Faces $380K Fine for Exposing Employees to Unprotected Trench
item.description: Department of Labor has cited a Frankfort, Illinois-based utility construction company for repeatedly exposing employees to excavation safety hazards after federal investigators observed employees working in an unprotected trench. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration initiated an investigation of Always Underground LLC as part of its National Emphasis Program on Trenching after witnessing employees working in an unprotected trench deeper than eight feet. OSHA cited the employer for three repeat violations for failing to provide workers with a safe means of egress, to install a trench protective system that would protect against cave-ins, and to keep excavated or other materials and equipment at least 2 feet from the edge.

item.title: FEMA Won’t Help Texas After July 2026 Floods
item.description: The Federal Emergency Management Agency has denied a request for federal aid to individuals needing help after the July 2026 floods in Texas, which swamped homes in Uvalde and damaged properties across Kerr County — in some cases for a second time in two years. “FEMA individual assistance was the big thing people were counting on and looking towards to be able to help them rebuild in a significant way,” said Allison Brim-Estelle, a field director with a national association for disaster survivors called Rebuild. FEMA said in a statement it was committed to helping the state recover and reviews requests for help closely, including by considering factors such as insurance coverage, other recent disasters, the profile of the population impacted, disaster-related unemployment and state fiscal capacity.

item.title: Delivery Robots Accused of Sharing Biometric Data Without Consent
item.description: The battle over Chicago’s food delivery robots has reached the courts, with two customers accusing the companies behind them of collecting their biometric data without consent. He says Coco did not tell him in writing that it would collect his biometric information, explain how long it would keep the data or obtain his written consent. The lawsuits accuse the companies of violating the Illinois Biometric Privacy Act, which requires companies collecting biometric data to provide written notice explaining what they collect and why, obtain written consent and maintain a policy for retaining and destroying the data.

item.title: Acrisure appoints Andy Tedstone as UK Retail CEO
item.description: Acrisure has appointed Andy Tedstone as chief executive officer of its UK Retail business, effective April 2027, as the global insurance and financial services group looks to strengthen its UK operations and accelerate growth. In his new role, Tedstone will focus on sustainable growth, strengthening client relationships and developing Acrisure’s UK retail proposition, combining local market expertise with the group’s international scale and capabilities. Jason Howard, president of International Insurance Solutions and Global Markets at Acrisure, said Tedstone’s experience and track record of building successful businesses would support the company’s continued investment in its UK retail operations.

item.title: Bracely raises $700,000
item.description: Bracely Insurance , a California startup developing a prevention-focused home insurance model, has raised $700,000 from 24 investors, according to an SEC filing. Founded in 2025, Bracely aims to connect home insurance pricing with property improvements and active monitoring. The financing was structured through Simple Agreements for Future Equity, with the first sale dated April 9, 2026.

item.title: RISK acquires majority stake in Vergelijkdirect.com
item.description: Dutch insurance distributor and financial products advisor RISK Ventures has acquired a majority stake in Vergelijkdirect.com, a Soest-based platform for comparing and purchasing personal and business insurance. The acquisition expands RISK’s online distribution capabilities, particularly in business insurance, as it seeks to grow its digital and offline distribution of business financial products. Vergelijkdirect.com will continue operating as a standalone entity, with its existing team and management retaining operational leadership.

item.title: Money Managers Say There’s Nowhere to Hide as Super El Niño Forms
item.description: The prospect of the world’s strongest ever El Niño cycle has a growing number of money managers racing to prepare their portfolios for the disruption they say is coming. “There is not a single place in the world that will not feel some kind of a knock-on effect from El Niño.” Strategies to navigate the shocks ahead span bets on interest rates tied to an El Niño-fueled bump in inflation. No corner of global asset markets will be fully shielded from the current El Niño cycle, says Katie Self, a portfolio manager at Pictet Asset Management.

item.title: Tesla Aiming Sell Cybercab Robotaxis by End of Year Despite Federal Probe
item.description: Tesla is aiming to start selling its Cybercab robotaxis to the public by the end of this year, its engineering chief said on Wednesday, even as the US auto safety agency probes the vehicles that come without manual controls which federal regulations typically require. Related: Appeals Court Blocks Class Actions Over Tesla’s Self-Driving Claims “We’re trying to get Cybercabs to customers by the end of this year, 2026,” he said. “As we start small this year, and we learn … about delivery and ownership and fleet management of autonomous vehicles in customer hands, we’ll continue to scale that.” After years of missed promises by Musk, Tesla started offering paid rides on a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin, Texas, early last month amid a frenzy of fans and social media influencers.

item.title: Companies, Governments Fight Hacking Attempts in Rush to Patch PHP Flaws
item.description: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed. As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare. The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand.

item.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
item.description: Slingshot Insurance , an AI-native embedded insurance startup, is emerging from stealth with $27 million in seed funding, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively. Slingshot, which is led by first-time founder and CEO Ethan Genteman , focuses on small insurance policies that consumers can buy as part of another purchase, such as coverage when booking a flight. The startup’s software helps businesses offer those policies by connecting them with insurers that back the coverage.

item.title: Hannover Re raises Acorn Re parametric cat bond target size again, to $450m
item.description: Hannover Re has for a second time increased the target size of what will be the seventh catastrophe bond offering in the annual Acorn Re parametric US earthquake series of deals, now seeking $450 million of limit from the Acorn Re Ltd. Hannover Re returned to market with this new and now seventh Acorn Re parametric catastrophe bond earlier this month , initially seeking $200 million of risk transfer and reinsurance limit for the single named ceding insurer, Oak Tree Assurance Ltd. Now, sources have told us the target size has been further increased, with $450 million of parametric earthquake reinsurance limit now being sought.

item.title: USAA lowers pricing again for still $350m Residential Re 2026-2 cat bond
item.description: US military mutual insurer USAA’s new Residential Reinsurance 2026 Limited (Series 2026-2) catastrophe bond issuance remains at the upsized $350 million target size, but the company seeks to capitalise on investor appetite and has lowered and adjusted the price guidance for the notes on offer again, Artemis has learned. So, the Residential Reinsurance 2026 Limited special purpose vehicle continues to offer three tranches of Series 2026-2 occurrence catastrophe bond notes to investors, with the proceeds set to be used to collateralize underlying reinsurance agreements between the issuing vehicle and sponsor USAA. With USAA once again lowering and adjusting the price of the notes on offer, it clearly shows that the insurer is looking to capitalise on catastrophe bond investor appetite to potentially gain more reinsurance support from the capital markets at more attractive pricing, from its latest cat bond sponsorship.

item.description: This third panel session of the day was titled “Beyond peak risk: The expanding spectrum of diversification in ILS.” The discussion was expertly moderated by Harry White , Head of PCS, Verisk Insurance Solutions. This new video features the third panel discussion of the day at our recent Artemis London 2026 catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities conference, a session focused on achieving diversification within the cat bond and ILS asset class and what that actually means for investors. Our Artemis London 2026 conference, the fifth in the series, was held on September 1st and around 220 attendees came through the door on the day to hear a range of insightful discussions from insurance-linked securities and reinsurance market leaders.

item.title: Texas Camp Hit by Floods Must Have New Manager, Judge Says
item.description: Camp Mystic , the Texas girls camp where 28 people were killed in flash floods last summer, must have a new management team to replace the family blamed for the deaths and settle lawsuits filed against the company, a judge ruled. US Bankruptcy Judge Christopher Lopez said that if the family of Richard Eastland, who co-owned and ran the company before he died in the flood, does not agree to give power to settle the lawsuits to an “independent fiduciary” the court will impose a government-approved trustee to run Camp Mystic. Company officials “must now choose whether they will implement independent oversight voluntarily or have the Court appoint a Chapter 11 Trustee.” Lopez rejected two competing proposals for how to manage the conflicts-of-interest involving Eastland family members who manage the camp.

item.title: US Says Screwworm Spreads to Wildlife for First Time
item.description: New World screwworm has been found in an elk in Texas, marking the first confirmed case of the potentially deadly animal parasite in US wildlife. “Hunters and others who spend time outdoors near infested areas are often among the first people to encounter affected wildlife, making their observations especially valuable to surveillance and response efforts,” the USDA said in Wednesday’s statement . Screwworm was first detected in Texas livestock in early June.

item.title: Florida Commissioner Orders Unlicensed Home, Auto Warranty Firms to Cease Ops
item.description: Florida’s insurance commissioner has ordered a home warranty company and an auto warranty firm to cease operations after finding they were not fully licensed in the state. “These suspensions are the result of two market conduct examinations that found iDeal Group, Inc., d/b/a iDeal Auto and First Premier Home Warranty Corp. The home warranty firm had entered into 207 home warranty contracts in Florida in 2023 through 2026, collecting premiums of almost $108,500.

item.title: Brown & Brown introduces COMPASS insurance intelligence platform
item.description: Brown & Brown has introduced COMPASS, an initiative combining its proprietary data, analytics, insurance expertise, and AI capabilities to support risk assessment, insurance purchasing, and portfolio optimisation. The brokerage expects COMPASS-powered knowledge assistants and business intelligence tools to reach thousands of employees by the end of 2026, starting in the US. In another example, the company said COMPASS analytics helped a Fortune 50 customer restructure its insurance program, cutting premium spending by 65% while substantially reducing potential risk volatility.

item.title: Globe Life premiums rise 7% as quarterly profit falls
item.description: Globe Life reported third-quarter net income of $361.1 million, down from $387.8 million a year earlier, while premium revenue rose 7% to $1.31 billion. Health insurance premiums increased 16% to $446.9 million, while life insurance premiums grew 2% to $864.6 million. Globe Life adjusted its full-year 2026 operating earnings guidance to $15.35–$15.65 per share, citing those health insurance issues.

item.title: Introducing Menlo Insurance Services
item.description: Menlo Insurance Services, operated by San Francisco-based Opero Labs, is an independent insurance brokerage offering commercial and personal coverage, with an option to handle insurance quote requests through AI assistants. The brokerage markets coverage including general liability, workers’ compensation, commercial auto, homeowners and specialty insurance for hard-to-place risks. Customers submit their information, and Menlo shops insurers and helps them compare coverage.

item.title: MSI partners with Moved
item.description: MGA MSI announced a new collaboration with Moved, a proptech platform for automating resident moves and ancillary revenue. As part of the partnership, MSI’s renters insurance will be embedded into the Moved platform, and compliance is tracked via the LeaseTrack technology offered through MSI. More than 4,000 properties and over 1 million units nationwide use Moved.

item.title: GM Targets ‘Eyes-Off’ Autonomous Driving for Pickups, SUVs
item.description: General Motors plans to offer “eyes-off” autonomous driving on its highest-selling, most profitable vehicles — big pickup trucks and SUVs — as it seeks fresh revenue streams from heavy technology investments. Last year, GM said it would offer autonomous highway driving in 2028 on its pricey but light-selling Cadillac Escalade IQ, an electric SUV. Some industry executives have said eyes-off driving that exchanges control back and forth from the car to the driver raises thorny safety and liability questions, and might not interest enough car shoppers.

item.title: Mexico gets its first World Bank Cat DDO, to complement cat bonds and parametric insurance
item.description: The Government of Mexico has received its first World Bank Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO), which will help the country prepare better and respond more quickly to natural disasters, while also complementing both of its IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 and IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) catastrophe bonds and parametric insurance protection. The World Bank Group has approved US $500 million in financing, marking the first time Mexico has accessed a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO). We are proud to support the Government of Mexico in this first Cat DDO,” commented Juan Pablo Uribe, World Bank Director for Mexico, Central America, and the Dominican Republic.

item.title: US Urges Fix for Widely Used Software After Critical Alerts
item.description: The US government is working to address and stop any potential cybersecurity issues stemming from flaws in PHP, a widely used open-source software, that may impact federal agencies and American critical infrastructure, according to a White House official. The programming language, called PHP, contains two vulnerabilities which could potentially expose organizations using it in websites and software platforms to cyberattacks. The developers responsible for maintaining PHP said Wednesday they released software updates to patch the vulnerabilities, urging users to adopt those changes immediately.
